passages.text: This is the vision of Obadiah: This is what the Lord GOD says about Edom— We have heard a message from the LORD; an envoy has been sent among the nations to say, “Rise up, and let us go to battle against her!”— “Behold, I will make you small among the nations; you will be deeply despised.
passages.sermon:
Obadiah received a vision from God.
The Lord GOD spoke about Edom.
We heard a message from the LORD.
God sent an envoy among the nations.
The envoy said, “Rise up.
Let us go to battle against Edom.”
God said, “I will make you small among the nations.
You will be deeply despised.”
passages.original: חֲז֖וֹן עֹֽבַדְיָ֑ה כֹּֽה־ אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה לֶאֱד֗וֹם שְׁמוּעָ֨ה שָׁמַ֜עְנוּ מֵאֵ֤ת יְהוָה֙ וְצִיר֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם שֻׁלָּ֔ח ק֛וּמוּ וְנָק֥וּמָה עָלֶיהָ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃ הִנֵּ֥ה קָטֹ֛ן נְתַתִּ֖יךָ בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם בָּז֥וּי אַתָּ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: The pride of your heart has deceived you, O dwellers in the clefts of the rocks whose habitation is the heights, who say in your heart, ‘Who can bring me down to the ground?’
passages.sermon:
Obadiah speaks a vision from the Lord God about Edom.
The Lord addresses the people of Edom.
You live in the clefts of the rocks.
Your home is set high above the ground.
You are proud in your heart.
Your pride has deceived you.
You say in your heart, “Who can bring me down to the ground?”
passages.original: זְד֤וֹן לִבְּךָ֙ הִשִּׁיאֶ֔ךָ שֹׁכְנִ֥י בְחַגְוֵי־ סֶּ֖לַע מְר֣וֹם שִׁבְתּ֑וֹ אֹמֵ֣ר בְּלִבּ֔וֹ מִ֥י יוֹרִדֵ֖נִי אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Though you soar like the eagle and make your nest among the stars, even from there I will bring you down,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to Edom.
The Lord is powerful.
You may rise high like an eagle.
You may place your nest among the stars.
Even if you go that high, I will bring you down.
The Lord has declared this.
passages.original: אִם־ תַּגְבִּ֣יהַּ כַּנֶּ֔שֶׁר וְאִם־ בֵּ֥ין כּֽוֹכָבִ֖ים שִׂ֣ים קִנֶּ֑ךָ מִשָּׁ֥ם אוֹרִֽידְךָ֖ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “If thieves came to you, if robbers by night— oh, how you will be ruined— would they not steal only what they wanted? If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings?
passages.sermon:
Thieves sometimes come at night.
Robbers sometimes attack in darkness.
If thieves came to you, they would only take what they wanted.
If robbers came, they would not take everything.
If grape gatherers came to you, they would leave some grapes behind.
You will be ruined far worse than this.
Your loss will be complete.
passages.original: אִם־ גַּנָּבִ֤ים בָּאֽוּ־ לְךָ֙ אִם־ שׁ֣וֹדְדֵי לַ֔יְלָה אֵ֣יךְ נִדְמֵ֔יתָה הֲל֥וֹא יִגְנְב֖וּ דַּיָּ֑ם אִם־ בֹּֽצְרִים֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔ךְ הֲל֖וֹא יַשְׁאִ֥ירוּ עֹלֵלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: But how Esau will be pillaged, his hidden treasures sought out!
passages.sermon:
Esau is a nation.
Enemies will search Esau.
They will find Esau’s hidden treasures.
They will take everything from Esau.
passages.original: אֵ֚יךְ נֶחְפְּשׂ֣וּ עֵשָׂ֔ו נִבְע֖וּ מַצְפֻּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: All the men allied with you will drive you to the border; the men at peace with you will deceive and overpower you. Those who eat your bread will set a trap for you without your awareness of it.
passages.sermon:
The people of Edom had allies.
These allies made agreements with Edom.
All the men allied with Edom will drive Edom to the border.
The men who were at peace with Edom will deceive Edom.
These men will overpower Edom.
Those who eat bread with Edom will set a trap for Edom.
Edom will not know about the trap.
Edom will not understand what is happening.
passages.original: עַֽד־ הַגְּב֣וּל שִׁלְּח֗וּךָ כֹּ֚ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י בְרִיתֶ֔ךָ הִשִּׁיא֛וּךָ יָכְל֥וּ לְךָ֖ אַנְשֵׁ֣י שְׁלֹמֶ֑ךָ לַחְמְךָ֗ יָשִׂ֤ימוּ מָזוֹר֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יךָ אֵ֥ין תְּבוּנָ֖ה בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: In that day, declares the LORD, will I not destroy the wise men of Edom and the men of understanding in the mountains of Esau?
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
He makes a promise about a future day.
The LORD will act on that day.
The LORD will destroy the wise men of Edom.
The LORD will remove understanding from the mountains of Esau.
passages.original: הֲל֛וֹא בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֤י חֲכָמִים֙ מֵֽאֱד֔וֹם וּתְבוּנָ֖ה מֵהַ֥ר עֵשָֽׂו׃

passages.text: Then your mighty men, O Teman, will be terrified, so that everyone in the mountains of Esau will be cut down in the slaughter.
passages.sermon:
Teman is a region in Edom.
The people of Teman are known for their strong warriors.
God will cause the mighty men of Teman to become afraid.
They will lose their courage.
Everyone in the mountains of Esau will be killed in the slaughter.
No one will escape.
passages.original: וְחַתּ֥וּ גִבּוֹרֶ֖יךָ תֵּימָ֑ן לְמַ֧עַן יִכָּֽרֶת־ אִ֛ישׁ מֵהַ֥ר עֵשָׂ֖ו מִקָּֽטֶל׃

passages.text: Because of the violence against your brother Jacob, you will be covered with shame and cut off forever.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Edom.
Edom acted violently against Jacob, his brother.
Because of this violence, shame will cover Edom.
God will cut off Edom forever.
passages.original: מֵחֲמַ֛ס אָחִ֥יךָ יַעֲקֹ֖ב תְּכַסְּךָ֣ בוּשָׁ֑ה וְנִכְרַ֖תָּ לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: On the day you stood aloof while strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gate and cast lots for Jerusalem, you were just like one of them.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Edom through the prophet Obadiah.
Edom is the nation descended from Esau.
Edom acted against Israel, who are the descendants of Jacob.
On a certain day, strangers attacked Jerusalem.
Strangers took away Jerusalem’s wealth.
Foreigners entered the gates of Jerusalem.
Foreigners cast lots for Jerusalem.
You, Edom, stood by and did nothing.
You watched while this happened.
You did not help your brother Jacob.
You acted just like the enemies of Jerusalem.
You became like one of those who harmed Jerusalem.
passages.original: בְּיוֹם֙ עֲמָֽדְךָ֣ מִנֶּ֔גֶד בְּי֛וֹם שְׁב֥וֹת זָרִ֖ים חֵיל֑וֹ וְנָכְרִ֞ים בָּ֣אוּ שַׁעֲרוֹ וְעַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ יַדּ֣וּ גוֹרָ֔ל גַּם־ אַתָּ֖ה כְּאַחַ֥ד מֵהֶֽם׃

passages.text: But you should not gloat in that day, your brother’s day of misfortune, nor rejoice over the people of Judah in the day of their destruction, nor boast proudly in the day of their distress.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Edom about their actions toward Israel, their brother nation.
Do not look with pleasure on your brother’s day of misfortune.
Do not rejoice over the people of Judah when they are destroyed.
Do not boast or speak proudly in the day of their trouble.
passages.original: וְאַל־ תֵּ֤רֶא בְיוֹם־ אָחִ֙יךָ֙ בְּי֣וֹם נָכְר֔וֹ וְאַל־ תִּשְׂמַ֥ח לִבְנֵֽי־ יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּי֣וֹם אָבְדָ֑ם וְאַל־ תַּגְדֵּ֥ל פִּ֖יךָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָֽה׃

passages.text: You should not enter the gate of My people in the day of their disaster, nor gloat over their affliction in the day of their disaster, nor loot their wealth in the day of their disaster.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Edom about Judah.
God calls Judah "My people."
Do not enter the gate of My people when disaster comes to them.
Do not look at their trouble when disaster strikes them.
Do not take their wealth when disaster falls on them.
passages.original: אַל־ תָּב֤וֹא בְשַֽׁעַר־ עַמִּי֙ בְּי֣וֹם אֵידָ֔ם אַל־ תֵּ֧רֶא גַם־ אַתָּ֛ה בְּרָעָת֖וֹ בְּי֣וֹם אֵיד֑וֹ וְאַל־ תִּשְׁלַ֥חְנָה בְחֵיל֖וֹ בְּי֥וֹם אֵידֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Nor should you stand at the crossroads to cut off their fugitives, nor deliver up their survivors in the day of their distress.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people.
God warns them about their actions during times of trouble.
Do not stand at the crossroads.
Do not block the way of those who are escaping.
Do not hand over the survivors.
Do not betray them when they are in distress.
passages.original: וְאַֽל־ תַּעֲמֹד֙ עַל־ הַפֶּ֔רֶק לְהַכְרִ֖ית אֶת־ פְּלִיטָ֑יו וְאַל־ תַּסְגֵּ֥ר שְׂרִידָ֖יו בְּי֥וֹם צָרָֽה׃

passages.text: For the Day of the LORD is near for all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; your recompense will return upon your own head.
passages.sermon:
The Day of the LORD is coming soon.
This day is near for all nations.
God will judge every nation.
God will treat you as you have treated others.
God will repay you for what you have done.
Your reward will come back to you.
You will receive what you deserve.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ קָר֥וֹב יוֹם־ יְהוָ֖ה עַל־ כָּל־ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֙יתָ֙ יֵעָ֣שֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ גְּמֻלְךָ֖ יָשׁ֥וּב בְּרֹאשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: For as you drank on My holy mountain, so all the nations will drink continually. They will drink and gulp it down; they will be as if they had never existed.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the nations.
God calls Mount Zion His holy mountain.
You drank on My holy mountain.
All the nations will also drink.
They will drink again and again.
They will swallow it down.
They will become as if they never existed.
passages.original: כִּ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֤ר שְׁתִיתֶם֙ עַל־ הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֔י יִשְׁתּ֥וּ כָֽל־ הַגּוֹיִ֖ם תָּמִ֑יד וְשָׁת֣וּ וְלָע֔וּ וְהָי֖וּ כְּל֥וֹא הָיֽוּ׃

passages.text: But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be holy, and the house of Jacob will reclaim their possession.
passages.sermon:
Mount Zion is a holy mountain.
God will make Mount Zion a place of deliverance.
God will keep Mount Zion holy.
The house of Jacob is the people of Israel.
The house of Jacob will reclaim their possessions on Mount Zion.
passages.original: וּבְהַ֥ר צִיּ֛וֹן תִּהְיֶ֥ה פְלֵיטָ֖ה וְהָ֣יָה קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְיָֽרְשׁוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֵ֖ת מוֹרָֽשֵׁיהֶם׃

passages.text: Then the house of Jacob will be a blazing fire, and the house of Joseph a burning flame; but the house of Esau will be stubble— Jacob will set it ablaze and consume it. Therefore no survivor will remain from the house of Esau.” For the LORD has spoken.
passages.sermon:
The house of Jacob will become a fire.
The house of Joseph will become a flame.
The house of Esau will become stubble.
Jacob and Joseph will burn Esau like fire burns stubble.
Jacob and Joseph will consume Esau completely.
No one from the house of Esau will survive.
The LORD has spoken.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֩ בֵית־ יַעֲקֹ֨ב אֵ֜שׁ וּבֵ֧ית יוֹסֵ֣ף לֶהָבָ֗ה וּבֵ֤ית עֵשָׂו֙ לְקַ֔שׁ וְדָלְק֥וּ בָהֶ֖ם וַאֲכָל֑וּם וְלֹֽא־ יִֽהְיֶ֤ה שָׂרִיד֙ לְבֵ֣ית עֵשָׂ֔ו כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: Those from the Negev will possess the mountains of Esau; those from the foothills will possess the land of the Philistines. They will occupy the fields of Ephraim and Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
passages.sermon:
God promised to restore His people Israel.
He will give them back their land.
People from the Negev will take the mountains of Esau.
People from the foothills will take the land of the Philistines.
They will take the fields of Ephraim.
They will take the fields of Samaria.
The tribe of Benjamin will take Gilead.
passages.original: וְיָרְשׁ֨וּ הַנֶּ֜גֶב אֶת־ הַ֣ר עֵשָׂ֗ו וְהַשְּׁפֵלָה֙ אֶת־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְיָרְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־ שְׂדֵ֣ה אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְאֵ֖ת שְׂדֵ֣ה שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וּבִנְיָמִ֖ן אֶת־ הַגִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: And the exiles of this host of the Israelites will possess the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the exiles from Jerusalem who are in Sepharad will possess the cities of the Negev.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites are God's chosen people.
Some Israelites are exiles.
These exiles are part of a group called "this host."
These exiles will possess the land of the Canaanites.
This land stretches as far as Zarephath.
There are also exiles from Jerusalem.
Some of these Jerusalem exiles live in Sepharad.
These Jerusalem exiles will possess the cities of the Negev.
passages.original: וְגָלֻ֣ת הַֽחֵל־ הַ֠זֶּה לִבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֲשֶֽׁר־ כְּנַעֲנִים֙ עַד־ צָ֣רְפַ֔ת וְגָלֻ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּסְפָרַ֑ד יִֽרְשׁ֕וּ אֵ֖ת עָרֵ֥י הַנֶּֽגֶב׃

passages.text: The deliverers will ascend Mount Zion to rule over the mountains of Esau. And the kingdom will belong to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The deliverers will go up to Mount Zion.
They will judge the mountains of Esau.
The LORD will rule as king.
The kingdom will belong to the LORD.
passages.original: וְעָל֤וּ מֽוֹשִׁעִים֙ בְּהַ֣ר צִיּ֔וֹן לִשְׁפֹּ֖ט אֶת־ הַ֣ר עֵשָׂ֑ו וְהָיְתָ֥ה לַֽיהוָ֖ה הַמְּלוּכָֽה׃
